notes: The San Francisco City Planning Commission's minutes of its regular meetings of 1979, from volume 38 of the San Francisco Public Library's deposit at the Internet Archive (38minutesofsanfran1979san). Pages were split from the hOCR search text on the Internet Archive page index, counting the viewer page among the leaves scandata.xml does not mark addToAccessFormats=false, and every page is dated from the meeting header it sits under. Four kinds of finding: what the Commission decided about a property, dated to the meeting that decided it; what the minutes state stood on or occupied the property; dated past facts the minutes state about a building; and landmark actions. A proposal on its own is not a finding. A Board of Supervisors or Board of Permit Appeals action the minutes report without its own date is framed 'by' the date of the meeting that reported it. The minutes name applicants, owners, attorneys, objectors, commissioners and staff throughout; the reader spec (in research/sources/sf-planning-commission-minutes.md, under Reader spec) barred all of them from every field, and kept companies, institutions, named buildings and architects.

coverage.remaining: Every page of volume 38 (38minutesofsanfran1979san, labelled 1979) was read. It holds 34 regular meetings, 4 January to 20 December 1979 (that of 27 December was cancelled); gaps in the resolution numbers and the minutes' own references show that the meetings of 22 and 29 March, 5 and 19 April, 10 and 31 May, 12 and 19 July, 20 and 27 September, 4 and 18 October, and 1, 15 and 29 November and 6 December are not in the scan, though the minutes continue cases to and from several of them. Next: volume 39 (1980), then 40-58 (1994-2005).
coverage.note: 309 OCR pages of minutes text out of 346 viewer pages (348 scanned leaves; the filter kept every page with 40 or more four-letter words or a meeting header, and dropped only the library card, the digitization notice and one two-character page), read in one session by a single reader with no sub-agents; 34 meetings, each dated from its own header. The year is dominated by condominium conversions (the 12 April sitting alone decided 27 condominium subdivisions), the non-conforming gasoline stations of 19th Avenue and the Sunset, and the downtown towers argued over before Proposition O (Federal Reserve Bank, Crocker Galleria, 101 California).
